levels.title_en: Adjectives that do and do not change

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f sound, and साफ़ never takes an ending, so the phrase is two clean syllables.

learn.explanation_en: Only adjectives ending in -ा take three forms. Everything else is fixed: साफ़, गरम, सुंदर, खाली, भारी, लाल, सफ़ेद, नारंगी — none of them ever changes, whatever noun it describes. That is roughly half the adjectives from Module 4, so the agreement problem is a good deal smaller than it first looks. The test is one question long: does it end in -ा? If not, leave it alone.

examples.note: Masculine noun, and साफ़ is unchanged.
Feminine noun, and still unchanged.
Another fixed adjective, and another feminine noun.

common_error.why_en: साफ़ does not end in -ा, so it has no feminine form to take.

practice.question: ___ किताब
practice.explanation_en: साफ़ never changes, so the feminine noun makes no difference to it.

game.explanation_en: साफ़ has only one form, so any ending added to it is wrong.

items.pronunciation_notes: नई is two short syllables with no य sounded between them: na-ii.

learn.title_en: नया — the one that breaks the pattern
learn.explanation_en: नया means new, and it is the one adjective in common use whose forms are not what the pattern predicts. Where बड़ा gives बड़ी and बड़े, नया gives नई and नए — the य disappears entirely rather than staying put and taking an ending. The regularised नयी and नये do turn up in older writing, but नई and नए are the forms to learn and use.

examples.note: The य drops in the feminine.
And in the masculine plural as well.
Only the masculine singular keeps the य.

common_error.why_en: The regular pattern would give नयी, but this adjective is irregular and the standard feminine is नई.

practice.question: ___ किताब
practice.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, and this adjective's irregular feminine is नई.

game.explanation_en: किताब is feminine and singular, and the standard form is नई rather than the regular-looking नयी.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three words, and only the first carries an agreement ending: baṛaa saaf ghar.

learn.explanation_en: Adjectives stack up before the noun in Hindi as they do in English, and each one agrees on its own terms. In बड़ा साफ़ घर the first agrees because it ends in -ा, and the second does not because it does not. Nothing coordinates them — each simply looks at the noun and does whatever its own ending requires, which means a phrase can easily have one changing word and one fixed one side by side.

examples.note: One adjective agrees, the other does not.
The first changes for the feminine; the second stays put.
Masculine plural, and गरम still does not move.

common_error.why_en: बड़ा agrees because it ends in -ा; साफ़ does not, so adding an ending to it is wrong.

practice.question: बड़ी ___ किताब
practice.explanation_en: बड़ी has already agreed with किताब. साफ़ has no forms at all, so it stays as it is.

game.explanation_en: Only बड़ा has forms to choose between, and किताब is feminine, so it takes बड़ी.

summary.recap_en: This level split the adjectives into two groups. Those ending in -ा take three forms, everything else takes one, and नया is the single irregular case. Two adjectives before one noun each behave independently.
summary.next_up_en: Next: where adjectives sit in a sentence, and agreement across a whole clause.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three words with the verb last and unstressed, as it always is: ghar achchhaa hai.
items.gloss_en: an adjective after the noun, before the verb

learn.title_en: Two places an adjective can sit
learn.explanation_en: An adjective can sit directly before its noun — अच्छा घर, a good house — or it can sit after the noun and before the verb, where it makes a claim: घर अच्छा है, the house is good. The agreement is identical in both positions, so nothing new has to be learned. What changes is the job: the first names a thing, the second says something about it.

examples.note: Naming a thing.
Making a claim about it.
Both positions inside one sentence.

common_error.why_en: घर is masculine, so the adjective takes -ा wherever in the sentence it sits.

practice.question: घर ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: घर is masculine and singular, so the adjective is अच्छा in this position too.

game.explanation_en: घर is masculine singular, so the adjective takes -ा and the verb stays है.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four words, three of them carrying plural marking, and घर unchanged in the middle.

learn.explanation_en: A full sentence can carry agreement in four places: the demonstrative, the noun, the adjective and the verb. ये बड़े घर हैं marks the plural on three of them, since घर itself does not change — and getting any one of them wrong makes the whole sentence wrong. The reliable way to build these is from the noun outwards: settle the noun and its number first, then let everything else follow from it.

examples.note: Three plural markers, with घर unchanged between them.
The same sentence in the singular.
Feminine, so the adjective does not change even in the plural.

common_error.why_en: The demonstrative and the verb are plural, so the adjective has to be plural too.

practice.question: ये ___ घर हैं।
practice.explanation_en: ये and हैं are both plural, so the adjective must take -े as well.

game.explanation_en: Only one option keeps the demonstrative, the adjective and the verb all plural at the same time.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both ठंडी and थी end in the same long ii, which makes the agreement audible as a rhyme.
items.gloss_en: agreement when the verb is past

learn.title_en: Agreement when the verb is past
learn.explanation_en: In the present the verb agrees with person and ignores gender entirely, so an adjective can be feminine while the verb looks exactly as it always does. In the past both agree, and both agree with the same noun. चाय ठंडी थी carries two feminine markers doing the same job, one after the other. That is why a wrong gender in the past costs two errors rather than one, and why it is so audible.

examples.note: Adjective and verb both feminine, and both rhyming.
The same structure, both masculine.
Feminine plural — only the verb shows the number.

common_error.why_en: Both the adjective and the verb agree with चाय, so both have to be feminine.

practice.question: चाय ठंडी ___।
practice.explanation_en: चाय is feminine and singular, so the past form is थी.

game.explanation_en: Both words have to be feminine. Two of these get one right and the other wrong, which is the commonest slip.

summary.recap_en: This level took agreement across the whole sentence. An adjective behaves the same before its noun as after it, a plural sentence can carry three or four plural markers, and in the past the adjective and the verb agree together.
summary.next_up_en: Next: postpositions, and sentences that finally get longer than three words.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dot nasalises the vowel, so में is a single hummed syllable with no n sounded.

learn.explanation_en: Hindi puts its little location words after the noun rather than before it. English says 'in the house'; Hindi says घर में, house-in. Words like this are called postpositions, and they are the biggest change to sentence shape you have met so far. में means in or inside, and it never changes form itself — a relief after the last two levels.

examples.note: The postposition follows the noun.
The same order with a feminine noun.

examples.english: There is sugar in the tea.
examples.note: A full sentence, and the verb is still last.

common_error.why_en: Postpositions come after the noun in Hindi, never before it.

practice.question: चाय ___ चीनी है।
practice.explanation_en: The sugar is inside the tea, so the postposition is में.

game.explanation_en: The postposition follows the noun, and में means inside. घर पर would mean 'at home'.

items.pronunciation_notes: A single tap for र and the final vowel drops: par, one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: पर means on, and also at when you mean stationed somewhere rather than inside it: मेज़ पर is on the table, घर पर is at home. It follows the noun like every postposition and never changes. One thing to note for later: पर is also a conjunction meaning 'but'. Position separates them — the conjunction sits between clauses, while the postposition sits right after a noun.

examples.note: The postposition follows the noun.
पर rather than में when you mean 'at' rather than 'inside'.

examples.english: There is a book on the table.
examples.note: The verb still comes last.

common_error.why_en: में means inside. A book resting on a table needs पर.

practice.question: मेज़ ___ किताब है।
practice.explanation_en: The book is resting on the table, so the postposition is पर.

game.explanation_en: पर is the right postposition for something resting on a surface, and it follows the noun.

items.pronunciation_notes: A flat ए with no glide: se, one syllable, and identical in sound to the से of कौन से.

learn.explanation_en: से covers a good deal of ground: from a place, with an instrument, by a means. घर से is from the house; हाथ से is by hand. You have already met this shape once, in कौन से — but that से is the plural of सा and has nothing whatever to do with this one. They are separate words that happen to be spelled alike, and only what surrounds them tells you which is which.

examples.note: Movement away, or origin.
The same word marking an instrument instead.
A full sentence, with the verb still at the end.

common_error.why_en: वह is singular, so the verb is है. A postposition does not change the agreement.

practice.question: वह स्कूल ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: से marks where someone or something comes from.

game.question_en: Which sentence means 'He is from the school'?
game.explanation_en: वह is singular so the verb is है, and से marks origin. वह स्कूल का है would mean it belongs to the school.

summary.recap_en: This level introduced postpositions — the little words that come after the noun instead of before it. में, पर and से never change form, and the verb still stays at the end of the sentence.
summary.next_up_en: Next: को, तक, and the one postposition that does change form.

items.pronunciation_notes: A flat ओ with no glide: ko, one syllable and unstressed.
items.gloss_en: to; and a marker for definite objects

learn.explanation_en: को marks a destination, and it also marks a person or definite thing that something is done to. That second use becomes important much later, when it changes how verbs agree. For now, treat it as 'to'. One warning worth having early: को is the postposition that most often forces a noun into a second form, which is what the whole next module is about — so the examples here stick to nouns that stay the same.

examples.note: A person as the destination.
घर is unchanged before को.
So is बाज़ार.

common_error.why_en: को follows the noun, like every other postposition.

practice.prompt_en: Complete the phrase meaning 'to the market'.
practice.question: बाज़ार ___
practice.explanation_en: को marks the destination. में would mean inside the market instead.

game.explanation_en: को follows the noun and marks the destination. से would mean 'from Ram'.

items.pronunciation_notes: A dental त with the tongue on the teeth, and the final vowel drops: tak.

learn.explanation_en: तक marks a limit, in space or in time: घर तक is as far as the house, रात तक is until night. It pairs naturally with से, which marks the starting point, and the two together cover most of what you need for describing stretches — सुबह से रात तक, from morning until night. Neither one changes form.

examples.note: A limit in space.
A limit in time.
से for the start, तक for the end.

common_error.why_en: तक follows the noun it limits, like every postposition.

practice.question: रात ___
practice.explanation_en: तक marks the end point. रात से would mean 'from night' instead.

game.question_en: Which phrase means 'from morning until night'?
game.explanation_en: से marks the start and तक the end, and each follows its own noun.

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable and unstressed, so in speech it leans onto the word before it: kaa.
items.gloss_en: of — and the postposition that agrees

learn.title_en: का — of, and the one that agrees
learn.explanation_en: का marks possession, and it is the odd one out among postpositions. While में, पर, से, को and तक never change, का takes three forms — का, के, की. And it agrees not with the owner but with the thing owned. राम का घर takes का because घर is masculine; राम की किताब takes की because किताब is feminine. Whose it is makes no difference at all, which is exactly the trap English speakers fall into.

examples.note: घर is masculine, so का.
किताब is feminine, so की — even though Ram is not.
Masculine plural, so के.

common_error.why_en: का agrees with the thing owned, and किताब is feminine. The owner's gender is irrelevant.

practice.question: राम ___ किताब
practice.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, so का takes its feminine form की.

game.explanation_en: का agrees with किताब, which is feminine, and not with राम.

summary.recap_en: This level added को, तक and का. The first two never change, but का takes three forms and agrees with the thing owned rather than with the owner — which is where Module 4's genders start paying for themselves.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the compound postpositions built on के, including the way Hindi says 'have'.

levels.title_hi: के लिए, के पास, के साथ

items.pronunciation_notes: Two short unstressed words, and लिए is said 'lie' in two quick syllables.

learn.explanation_en: Some postpositions are built from का plus another word, and के लिए is the commonest of them: it means 'for'. The का part is frozen in its के form here and does not agree with anything at all — that is the whole point of these compounds. Once you learn to spot the के at the front, the rest of the group becomes recognisable on sight.

examples.note: The के does not agree with anything.
The same frozen form before a masculine noun.
Feminine noun, and still के.

common_error.why_en: In के लिए the के is fixed and does not agree with the noun before it.

practice.question: किताब ___ लिए
practice.explanation_en: In this compound the के never changes, whatever noun comes before it.

game.explanation_en: के लिए is a fixed pair. Unlike plain का, it does not agree with anything.

items.pronunciation_notes: पास has a long aa and the final vowel drops: ke paas, two syllables.

learn.title_en: के पास — near, and how Hindi says 'have'
learn.explanation_en: के पास means near or beside, but it does a second and far more important job. Hindi has no verb 'to have', and के पास with होना is how possession is expressed instead. राम के पास किताब है is literally 'near Ram a book is' and means 'Ram has a book'. Watch what the verb agrees with: the thing owned, not the owner. That will keep being true, and it is the first sign of a pattern Module 10 is built on.

examples.note: The plain meaning of location.
The verb agrees with किताब, not with राम.
A plural thing owned, so a plural verb.

common_error.why_en: The verb agrees with किताब, which is singular — not with राम.

practice.question: राम के पास किताबें ___।
practice.explanation_en: किताबें is plural, and the verb agrees with the thing owned rather than with राम.

game.explanation_en: The verb must match किताब. के पास is also a fixed pair, so की पास is never right.

items.pronunciation_notes: साथ ends in an aspirated dental थ, with the tongue on the teeth and breath released.
items.setting_en: Two friends at a tea stall, looking at what is on offer

learn.explanation_en: के साथ means 'with' in the sense of company — alongside someone or something. Do not confuse it with से, which also translates as 'with' but means by means of: हाथ से is with your hand as a tool, राम के साथ is with Ram as company. English uses one word for both and Hindi does not, so this is a distinction you have to make deliberately. The exchange below uses two of the compound postpositions side by side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.english: What is there with the tea?

lines.speaker: B
lines.english: There are sweets with the tea.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: और राम के पास क्या है?
lines.read_as: aur raam ke paas kyaa hai?

common_error.why_en: के साथ is a fixed pair and the के never agrees, even before a feminine noun like चाय.

practice.question: चाय ___ साथ मिठाई है।
practice.explanation_en: के साथ is fixed, so the के stays even though चाय is feminine.

game.question_en: Listen to the second line. Which word is missing?
game.mask_reason: the frozen के of a compound postposition
game.explanation_en: In compound postpositions the के never changes, so a feminine noun before it makes no difference.

tts_strings: और राम के पास क्या है?

summary.recap_en: This level covered the compound postpositions built on के. All of them freeze the के rather than agreeing, and के पास carries the whole weight of 'have' in a language that has no such verb.
summary.next_up_en: Next: negation, word order, and the connectors that join two sentences.
